_comment: Baselines for scripts/screenshot.sh. Numbers here are measurements from a real run, not hand-picked targets. Regenerate with `scripts/screenshot.sh --update` after a deliberate visual change, then read the printed diff before committing — a diff that isn't explained by your change means something regressed. The app is run against a throwaway seeded library, so every number below is a measurement of src/seed.rs rendered by this repository and of nothing else; it used to be read out of whoever's real library happened to be on the machine, which made the net go red for reasons no diff could show. Keep this file formatted exactly as `jq .` emits it: --update rewrites it through jq, so matching jq's formatting is what keeps an --update diff down to the numbers that actually changed.

logical_window.note: The logical (CSS-pixel) window the app asks for — WIDTH/HEIGHT in src/lib.rs. Every region below is written in these CSS pixels, the same units the source code uses, so a human can check `right: 36` against the `right: 20px` in src/screens/library.rs without doing arithmetic. The capture is physical pixels, so the script converts by a scale factor it derives as captured_height / 852. Height, not width, and that choice is load-bearing: the window manager is free to ignore the size the app asks for, and this one does — it has granted 491x1065 and later 550x1065 for the very same request, i.e. it stretched the width and left the height alone. 1065 = 852 x 1.25 exactly on this 1.25x display, so the height is the dimension that still carries the scale factor honestly; the width no longer does and must never be used to derive it. If a window manager ever starts stretching the height too, this derivation breaks and the right fix is to ask the compositor for the scale factor, not to re-record the numbers below.

region_schema.note: Every region states the edge of the *captured image* it hangs off, because the window manager decides the capture size and absolute WxH+X+Y coordinates slide off their target the moment it changes its mind. `anchor` is required and must be one of the six below; the offsets are CSS pixels measured inward from the anchored edge to the nearest edge of the region, and `w`/`h` are its CSS-pixel size.

anchors.top: spans the capture width; requires `top` and `w`: "full"
anchors.bottom: spans the capture width; requires `bottom` and `w`: "full"

region_schema.self_test: `scripts/screenshot.sh --self-test` resolves every region below against five capture sizes and asserts the arithmetic, without building or launching anything.

checks.name: thumb_painted
checks.description: The library's first row 38x38 attachment thumb is actually painted, not just laid out. Caught the display:contents paint regression (README: 'The paint regression') where boxes were sized correctly but never drawn.
checks.note: Reference: ~0.907 painted (grey fill over paper), ~0.970 unpainted (bare paper) — a delta far outside tolerance. Top-left anchored because the content column starts at the left edge: this region measures byte-identically at 491x1065 and 550x1065, which is the proof that a left anchor is the right one for it.

checks.name: fab_solid_accent
checks.description: The library FAB (bottom-right, add song) is filled solid with the accent colour.
checks.note: The FAB is `position: absolute; right: 20px; bottom: 16px; width: 60px; height: 60px` in src/screens/library.rs, so it hangs off the bottom-right corner and nothing else. Its `bottom: 16px` is measured from the Library screen box, which ends above the bottom nav, so the region's own `bottom: 96` is 16px plus the rendered height of the nav strip — a text metric, not a constant, and therefore measured rather than derived. Horizontally the region sits between `right: 36` and `right: 64`, which is inside the 20..80 the FAB occupies with room to spare on both sides. It is deliberately in the FAB's lower band: above it the plus glyph is drawn in the on-accent colour, and to its right the first visible song row's confidence dots can overlap the FAB entirely at narrower window widths — both are FAB pixels that are correctly not accent, and sampling either would make this check fail for the wrong reason. The 20px corner radius is cleared on all four sides.

checks.name: group_header_accent
checks.description: The first library group header's label (e.g. 'SOLID') is painted in the accent colour, not the muted grey later headers use.

checks.name: bottom_nav_accent
checks.description: The bottom nav strip carries the accent colour: the active item (Songs, selected by default) has its icon and its label painted in it, and it is the only thing in the strip that is ever accent — the inactive item is muted grey and the hairline and the paper are neither.
checks.note: Spans the whole capture width on purpose. The two nav items are `flex: 1`, so the active one re-centres over the left half whenever the window manager grants a different width — there is no fixed x it can be sampled at. Counting accent pixels across the full strip is the same assertion, because nothing else in the strip is accent; what it gives up is the ability to say *which* item is active, which this check never asserted in a way pixels could tell apart anyway.

checks.name: screen_background
checks.description: The screen background is the light-mode paper colour, sampled from the empty status-bar strip at the very top.
checks.note: The safe-area strip the OS status bar sits in. It is empty across the full width at every window size, so the top-left corner of it is background under any grant the window manager can make.

checks.name: background_has_no_accent
checks.description: NEGATIVE CONTROL. The opposite corner of that same empty status-bar strip contains no accent pixels at all. Nothing about the app can make this fail; only the checking machinery can.
checks.note: Every other check here is of the form 'this colour is present', and a suite made only of those passes just as happily when the colour comparison has quietly started matching everything — a stuck `compare`, an ImageMagick whose -fuzz argument changed meaning, a crop that silently resolves to the whole image. This one asserts the negative through the exact same sampling path, at the same 20% fuzz the accent-presence checks use, over a region that is guaranteed paper. If it ever goes red, do not look at the app: look at this script and at ImageMagick. It is also why --update refuses to re-record it — a control whose threshold is measured from the run it is meant to be policing is not a control.
